description: Three.js WebGL 3D scene starter on Vite with a renderer, camera, lit mesh, and resize loop wired from first render.

buildHints.whenToUse: 3D scene viewers, WebGL games, shader playgrounds, gltf/fbx asset explorers, or any product archetype where the primary surface is a live 3D canvas.
firstSteps: Install: `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173 with HMR, the cube should render immediately.
The full scene lives in `src/main.ts` — scene, camera, renderer, lights, mesh, and animation loop are all in one file so you can fork cleanly.
Add 3D models via `three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js` — place assets in `public/` (Vite serves it at the root) and load with `new GLTFLoader().load('/model.glb', ...)`.
Build: `pnpm build` emits static assets to `dist/` — deploy anywhere; there is no server.
For shaders, import `.glsl` as `?raw` or inline as template strings; there is no GLSL plugin by default.
gotchas: Canvas must be resized on window resize — call `renderer.setSize(w, h)` AND `camera.aspect = w/h; camera.updateProjectionMatrix()`. Setting only CSS width/height stretches the image and does not update the projection.
`renderer.setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio)` is required for sharp output on retina, but cap it at 2 — uncapped it tanks framerate on 3x phones.
`requestAnimationFrame` must be cancelled on teardown (HMR, route change), otherwise multiple loops run in parallel and CPU climbs. Store the handle and call `cancelAnimationFrame`.
Dispose geometries, materials, and textures manually when swapping scenes — three.js does not garbage-collect GPU memory. Use `geometry.dispose()`, `material.dispose()`, `texture.dispose()`.
architectureNotes: Single renderer, single scene, single render loop — do not create a new `WebGLRenderer` per frame or per component; it leaks the GL context.
Keep render-loop work pure: mutate transforms in the loop, construct meshes/materials outside it. Allocations inside the loop cause GC pauses visible as jank.

placeholders.description: Scene bootstrap — renderer, camera, lights, and a rotating cube plus resize + animation loop. Replace the cube with the product's actual geometry or `GLTFLoader` call; keep the resize + dispose plumbing.
